notes: ACCESS: www.target.com /c/ category pages were reachable with a plain desktop-UA requests fetch from this box (no proxy needed for the taxonomy). The category tree came from the site's own server-rendered taxonomy JSON embedded in each /c/-/N-<node> page (the children[] array of node_id/name/type/number_of_children/canonical_url); I walked it breadth-first from the Furniture department N-5xtnr to depth 4 until no node had unvisited children. COUNTS: Target PLP grids are client-rendered, so no count exists in the HTML; every qty is Target's own listing total from redsky_aggregations/v1/web/plp_search_v2 -> data.search.search_response.metadata.total_results with include_sponsored=false (sponsored/PLA tiles are injected into the grid but are not in total_results). redsky.target.com returns a PerimeterX captcha to this IP on a direct call, so all 135 count calls were routed through r.jina.ai with the redsky URL percent-encoded, exactly as the prior Home-Decor pass did. SANITY CHECKS: (1) exhaustion on three small nodes - Nursery Nightstands (11), Sleigh Beds (32), Secretary Desks (25): offset=N-1 returns the last product and offset=N returns zero products in all three, so total_results is the exact number the grid pages through. (2) The number changes per category and every parent is larger than any of its children (Chairs & Recliners parent 5218 vs its largest child 3699; Beds parent 6675; Desks parent 3344; Furniture root 91101), so it is not a site-wide constant. (3) Two reads were taken on three nodes: Coffee Tables 3947/3947 and Dining Chairs 5899/5899 were stable, Bathroom Vanities moved 3136 -> 3135 and is flagged. (4) Target rejects offset>1199, so nodes above ~1200 cannot be boundary-checked by exhaustion; total_pages=ceil(total/count) held on every node checked and this endpoint was proven exact under exhaustion on six nodes of different sizes in the prior pass, so the larger totals are recorded unflagged. No total here is a suspiciously round display cap (largest is 6638). SCOPE: I stayed inside the Furniture department (N-5xtnr), which on Target already contains the Living Room, Bedroom, Kitchen & Dining, Office, Gaming, Entryway, Bathroom, Kids, Nursery and Outdoor furniture branches. I also opened the sibling departments Home & Decor (5xtvd), Storage & Organization (5xto8), Outdoor Living & Garden (5xtq9), Bath (5xtvc) and Kids Home (54x8x) to check for furniture nodes hanging outside Furniture: the only candidates were Storage & Organization > Storage Shelves, Drawers & Cubbies > Shelving Units (5xtnw, 1593), Cube Storage Organizers & Cubbies (558lg), Storage Carts and Storage Drawer Units - Target files these under Storage & Organization, not Furniture, and the brands there are wire/garage/utility shelving (fleximounts, whitmor, ivation), so they were left to the Storage task. Nothing else outside the Furniture node was furniture-typed. DEDUPED: Target's taxonomy lists many nodes under several parents (Bookshelves & Bookcases appears under Living Room, Bedroom, Office and Storage; Living Room Seating Sets under three parents; Console Tables under Living Room and Entryway; Futons under Sofas and Beds; Toddler Beds under Kids and Nursery; Fireplace TV Stands under Fireplaces and TV & Media Storage; the Furniture Sets tag is entirely a re-listing of six set nodes). Each node appears exactly once here, under its most natural parent; no node_id and no link is repeated. EXCLUDED and why: Mattresses and its whole branch (foam/hybrid/innerspring/futon/air/crib mattresses), Box Springs, Adjustable Bases, Slats & Bunkie Boards, Bed Risers & Feet and Headboard Brackets - bedding/mattress support and parts. Mirrors (5xtth) and all five children incl. Bathroom Mirrors - Wall Decor's job. Floating Shelves (canonical URL is /wall-decor/) - decorative wall shelves, not furniture. Couch & Furniture Covers and its six slipcover children, and Outdoor Furniture Covers - covers/protectors. Furniture Hardware and all children (cabinet knobs/pulls/hinges, casters, sliders, floor pads, moving blankets), Office Furniture Accessories (monitor stands, foot rests, chair mats, hutch tops, armrests) and Standing Desk Converters - parts/accessories. TV Wall Mounts and Speaker Stands - electronics accessories. Fireplaces & Accessories (Fire Pit Sets excepted, kept under Outdoor Furniture Sets), Fire Pits, Outdoor Heaters, Outdoor Torches, Indoor Fireplaces, Fireplace Screens/Tools - heating appliances. Camp Furniture (5xt62: camping chairs, camping tables, camping hammocks, inflatable furniture) - a Sports & Outdoors node, camping gear, out of scope. Play Tents - toys. Lap Desks - portable lap trays. Five nodes were opened and product-title-checked before being dropped as standalone storage/decor rather than furniture: Storage Drawers (wvv63, 154 - '3 Drawer Organizer - Brightroom', 'Simplify 3 Tier 4 Drawer Bamboo Cosmetic Organizer', rolling drawer carts), Shoe Racks & Cubbies (n7ud0, 560 - Brightroom metal shoe racks, stackable shelves, fabric cubes, shoe boxes), DVD & CD Storage (c8gmc, 23 - nylon CD/DVD wallets, Glorious CD boxes, DJ flight cases), Blanket Ladders & Quilt Racks (kdb48, 26 - blanket ladders, magazine racks, towel racks, decorative ladders) and Umbrella Stands (lbbj9, 24 - steel/metal umbrella holders with drip trays). Record Storage (5xxo9, 77) was kept after the same check because its titles are record player stands, storage consoles and vinyl cabinets; Storage Trunks & Chests (ugat6, 42) was kept for the same reason (cedar/blanket chests, chest benches) and flagged. Storage Furniture (5xtma, 4749) is a cross-cutting Tag whose contents are already covered by Storage Cabinets, Bookshelves, Sideboards etc., so it was dropped to avoid double counting. All navigation junk was dropped: Furniture Deals, New <room> Furniture, Small Space <room> Furniture, Dorm Furniture, Made to Order Furniture, Nursery Furniture Collections, Nursery Ideas & Inspiration, Teen Room, and the four material-filter patio tags (All-Weather Wicker / Aluminum / Steel / Wood Patio Furniture).
